§ 2Content

§ 3JOINTS

  • A joint is a point or location where two or more bones meet, allowing for movement.
  • Joints are also called articulations; they are essential for flexibility and mobility in the skeletal system.

§ 4TYPES OF JOINTS

1. Synovial Joint

  • These joints have a fluid-filled cavity between the bones, allowing for a wide range of motion.
  • E.g. knee, elbow, shoulder (the most mobile joints).

2. Fibrous Joint

  • These joints connect bones with dense connective tissue, allowing for little to no movement.
  • E.g. sutures in the skull (the seams between skull bones); the connection between teeth and the jawbone.

3. Cartilaginous Joint

  • In these joints, bones are connected by cartilage, allowing for slight movement.
  • E.g. joints between vertebrae (in the spine); the connection between ribs and the sternum.

Quick Reference

Joint typeMovementExamples
SynovialWide rangeKnee, elbow, shoulder
FibrousLittle to noneSutures (skull), teeth-jaw
CartilaginousSlightVertebrae-vertebrae, ribs-sternum

§ 5Key concepts

  • Synovial (knee, elbow, shoulder) — wide motion, fluid cavity
  • Fibrous (skull sutures, teeth-jaw) — little/no motion
  • Cartilaginous (spine, ribs) — slight motion
